result.notes: The proposed prompt was already anatomically sound and topic-appropriate. Corrections made: (1) Added the round black pupil at the iris centre and clarified the lens sits directly behind the iris/pupil (the original placed the lens merely "encircled" by the iris, which reads ambiguously; the pupil is a defining, instantly-recognisable landmark). (2) Sharpened retina colour to reddish-orange and specified it lines the curved inner BACK wall, and the optic nerve exits the REAR — reinforcing correct posterior-segment anatomy. (3) Reinforced one-glance recognition by making the cutaway eyeball explicitly dominate the portrait frame. (4) Explicitly stated "blank markers only" on the pointer lines to guarantee NO readable words/labels (topic requires label lines only). (5) Confirmed Singapore multi-ethnic context (Singaporean-Chinese instructor) and forced scrubs to plain solid blue with no trim. No wrong or invented instruments were present; the six required structures (cornea, iris, lens, vitreous, retina, optic nerve) are all correctly depicted.

result.subject_final: Extreme macro of a warm brown elderly Singaporean-Chinese eye filling the frame, its dark iris ring staying sharp and richly coloured while the round pupil aperture is completely filled by a dense, frosted milky-white and amber opacity — a mature cataract reading as a solid pale-and-golden clouding seen through the pupil. Soft raking clinical light catches crisp lashes and natural crinkled skin, so the opaque, clouded pupil is unmistakably a cataract; a calm, unposed expression.
result.notes: The core sign is correct: a mature cataract presents as a milky white-to-amber opacity in the pupil (leukocoria / brunescent lens), which is the single canonical one-glance image for "Lens & Cataract Disorders" — an OA/OT/PSA names it instantly. FIX 1 (anatomy): the original said the opacified lens "glowing pale behind the iris." That is anatomically misleading — the iris is opaque, so the cataractous crystalline lens is only visible THROUGH the circular pupil, never seen behind the iris. I confined the opacity strictly to the round pupil aperture, with the coloured iris ring intact around it, which is exactly how a mature cataract actually looks. FIX 2 (Singapore context): specified an elderly Singaporean-Chinese subject to lock the multi-ethnic SG anchor for the visible skin/eye. No people-scene, staff, or scrubs appear (single-eye macro), so the plain-blue-scrubs rule is N/A. No text, logos, or camera references introduced. Kept the white-and-amber palette and raking clinical light so the frosted opaque pupil dominates the frame and reads as cataract in one glance.

result.subject_final: An extreme close-up of a healthy retinal fundus filling the entire frame: a glowing orange-red retina, a bright creamy pinkish-yellow circular optic disc set off to one side, and dark red blood vessels streaming outward from that disc in graceful superior and inferior arcs that sweep around a darker reddish-brown central macula left clear of large vessels.
